bench.reason: baseline 1.395 ms is below the 15 ms noise floor even at the largest bench scene (geo=400 array=20000); measured anyway -- every accept must clear 1.15x on two independent timings

ledger.hypothesis: the node is GRID-shaped (n=3 live shapes, resolution 2..13 per tick, 18..1670 verts): the cost was ~25 heap-allocated whole-array temporaries per shape per pass plus bounds-checked nd::at3 table lookups per cube, not the arithmetic; a fused loop with the reference's exact expression order is byte-identical and removes a level of work. Follow-ups in the same round: std::pow(x,2.0)->x*x in the box/cylinder kernels (numpy's **2 is np.square and LLVM folds it, MSVC's CRT pow does not -- 225->78 us on the sampler), and the per-shape decomposition/bounds lifted to scalars (68 us of nd allocations for 3 shapes).
ledger.note: confirmed twice (incumbent under the noise floor): 0.326 / 0.335 ms
ledger.risk: expression-order drift in the fused kernel (matrix_point accumulator start, smooth-union formula, +-0 through linspace) -- mitigated by keeping every expression verbatim and by a fingerprint A/B of outMesh against the original plug-in (identical values); MSVC pow(x,2) vs x*x could differ by 1 ulp in the OLD build only, the reference build (clang) already computed x*x
ledger.theme: collapse the per-shape nd::Array SDF sampling chain and the table-driven dual marching cubes into one raw per-grid-point loop, and stop reading the 20000-element arrays past the shape count that _dense_over truncates them to

ledger.hypothesis: instrumenting compute() showed the bench scene is 3 shapes on a ~27x16x16 grid (not 20000 shapes: the builtin scene trims the multis), with ~0.11 ms in the sampler, ~0.04 ms in DMC and ~0.15 ms in Maya's MFnMesh::create; the sampler is divider-throughput bound (3 div + sqrt per shape-point), so the only exact way to cut it is to not divide when the divisor is exactly 1.0 (x/1.0 == x for every x), which the identity-matrix scene hits on all three shapes; DMC's three passes reload the same field corners three times and grow fresh vectors every tick
ledger.note: confirmed twice (incumbent under the noise floor): 0.271 / 0.272 ms
ledger.risk: the fast path is gated on scale == 1.0 and min|scale| == 1.0 exactly, so a scaled shape takes the original divide path; the fused DMC relies on every quad neighbour offset being <= 0 so its cube index is already assigned in scan order, and vertices are appended in the same scan order as the old counting pass; mb_max/mb_min replace std::isnan(a) with a != a, which is the same predicate for IEEE doubles. The remaining ~0.15 ms is MFnMesh::create for ~800 quads, which no node-side change reaches; the grid size changes every tick (resolution moves) so no grid cache can hit on this bench.
ledger.theme: hoist the per-shape branches out of the grid loop, skip the three divisions when a shape's scale is exactly 1.0, fuse the three dual-marching-cubes passes into one scan, and keep the output buffers' capacity across ticks

ledger.hypothesis: at the bench's median tick (grid ~24x14x14, 3 shapes) the sampler is ~83 us of a ~241 us compute; a condvar pool with 8 threads should cut it to ~30 us, and a 2-thread pool to ~55 us
